deep.reconstruction: This page contains no calculation. It is a philosophical commentary that finishes §3 ('Stetigkeit der geraden Linie') of the draft of Dedekind's 'Stetigkeit und irrationale Zahlen' (1872). On the previous page Dedekind stated his continuity principle. In modern form: if the points of a line L are split into two non-empty classes A1 and A2, with A1 ∪ A2 = L, A1 ∩ A2 = ∅, and every a1 in A1 lying to the left of every a2 in A2, then there is exactly one point α that produces this cut. That point is either the greatest element of A1 or the least element of A2. This is the line-version of Dedekind completeness. On this page he makes the following points. (i) He expects readers to be disappointed that such a triviality is supposed to reveal the secret of continuity. (ii) He is glad if everyone finds the principle self-evident and in agreement with their idea of a line, because he cannot prove it and nobody can. (iii) Accepting this property is an axiom: through it we first ascribe continuity to the line, we 'think continuity into' the line. (iv) If space has a real existence, it need not be continuous. Countless of its properties would stay the same if it were discontinuous. (v) Even if we knew for certain that space were discontinuous, nothing would stop us, if we chose, from making it continuous in thought by filling its gaps. This filling, a 'creation of new point-individuals', would have to follow the principle above. Point (v) leads directly into §4, 'Schöpfung der irrationalen Zahlen', where the rationals are completed by cuts. The page's role is therefore methodological. It establishes continuity as an axiom, not a provable fact, and treats completion as a free mental creation governed by the cut principle. Nothing implicit needs to be filled in.
errors: No mathematical errors; the page makes no derivations. The philosophical claims (continuity of physical space is not provable, it is an axiom about the geometric line) agree with the published 1872 text and are coherent.

results.what: Continuity of the line is taken as an unprovable axiom: every cut of the line's points is produced by exactly one point.
results.modern_name: Dedekind completeness axiom (cut axiom), geometric form; cf. the continuity axioms in Hilbert's Grundlagen
results.usually_credited_to: Richard Dedekind, 'Stetigkeit und irrationale Zahlen' (1872; ideas dated by him to 1858)

results.what: Remark that real space need not be continuous, and that a discontinuous space could be completed in thought by creating new points according to the cut principle.
results.modern_name: Completion by cuts (Dedekind completion) as free creation; independence of continuity from other geometric properties

deep.surprise_reason: This is a draft of a well-known published passage, the end of §3 of 'Stetigkeit und irrationale Zahlen'. It is nearly word for word the 1872 text, apart from small revisions ('Axioms' replaced by 'Princips', added 'gewiß', 'wieder', 'in Gedanken'). Those revisions are of minor philological interest only.

checkable.asserts: The rationals have gaps (no rational square root of 2). This motivates the 'Ausfüllung der Lücken' mentioned here and carried out in §4; it is not itself on this page.

Line 7: a struck word after 'Linie' (possibly 'Stetigkeit'/'stetig'), illegible.
Lines 17-18: two fully struck lines after 'würden', illegible, followed by 'dieselben bleiben'.
'Und wüßten {gewiß} wir' — 'gewiß' is inserted above; 'wir' may be partly overwritten. The published version reads 'Und wüßten wir gewiß, daß der Raum unstetig wäre'.
'so könnte uns doch {wieder} Nichts hindern' — 'wieder' is inserted above 'doch'; the marginal 'falls es uns beliebte,' is keyed by a bracket into the line after 'hindern,'.
'Lücken [-...-] {in Gedanken} zu einem stetigen zu machen' — 'in Gedanken' is inserted above.

'diese Ausfüllung [-würde-] oder Schöpfung neuer Punkt-Individuen würde aber dem obigen Princip gemäß auszuführen sein' — the image matches; the published text rephrases this as 'würde aber in einer Schöpfung von neuen Punkt-Individuen bestehen'.
